summary.headline: Q2 FY27 consolidated EBITDA swung to a INR 848 million loss on INR 6,747 million revenue (down ~8% YoY), driven by Treatment Solutions legacy-project cost overruns.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 operating income was INR 6,747 million, down about 8% YoY, with EBITDA at a loss of INR 848 million and net loss after tax of INR 828 million. Management attributed the swing mainly to revised estimated cost-to-complete on certain legacy Treatment Solutions projects, which it said were fully provided for in the quarter and represented about 90% of the quarter's negative PBT. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 13,752 million (up just under 4%) with EBITDA loss of INR 530 million. Industrial Products, Specialty Chemicals and Consumer Products grew strongly in revenue, while Treatment Solutions revenue roughly halved and management guided to a second-half recovery.

segments.name: Treatment Solutions
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 1,498 million vs INR 2,958 million YoY; EBIT loss INR 1,215 million vs loss of INR 122 million. H1 revenue INR 3,597 million (vs INR 4,797 million) and EBIT loss INR 1,389 million.

segments.name: Industrial Products
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 1,360 million, up ~35% YoY; EBIT INR 86 million (vs INR 74 million). H1 revenue INR 2,411 million (up ~25%) and EBIT INR 210 million.

segments.name: Lifecycle Services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 706 million (vs INR 770 million YoY); EBIT INR 59 million. H1 revenue INR 1,422 million (vs INR 1,329 million) and EBIT INR 130 million.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 2,546 million, up ~17% YoY; EBIT INR 225 million. H1 revenue INR 4,843 million (up ~19%) and EBIT INR 448 million. Margins under pressure from West Asia input cost inflation and Roha plant facility costs (management attributed ~18% of margin decline to these factors plus lower exchange gains).

segments.name: Consumer Products
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 1,005 million, up ~30% YoY; EBIT loss INR 41 million (vs loss of INR 23 million). H1 revenue INR 2,129 million (up ~32%) with EBIT loss of INR 45 million.

guidance_outlook: Treatment Solutions: management expects H2 turnover improvement and better margins; expects full-year Treatment Solutions revenue to approach prior-year levels, with heavy invoicing in Q3 and Q4.
Treatment Solutions margins expected to return to higher single digits in the balance of the year; Q1-level margins to be maintained.
Engineering division revenue expected to return to about INR 1,750 crore (ex-intersegment) as in FY26; a clearer year-end outlook to be given after next quarter.
Roha plant backward integration expected to be complete within FY27; the legacy contract expected to spill into FY28 with no further material adverse impact assumed.
Consumer Products expected to reach break-even by end of FY27, though H1 was marginally below expectations.
Specialty Chemicals: price increases gaining traction domestically, slower internationally; margin recovery expected in coming months as input costs stabilise.
Membrane plant with Mann+Hummel tech tie-up in Goa expected to be up by end of FY27, with volumes from FY28.
capex_capacity: CWIP of about INR 240 crore at September 2026, largely for Roha backward-integration plant (commissioning expected by year end), plus modular expansion at Ankleshwar and membrane UF expansion in Goa.
Roha resin plant commissioned 30 September 2025; utilisation at about 25% in its first year, with management targeting ~25% annual utilisation growth.
Oman project is a JV; its CWIP will be consolidated and build up toward year end as retrofit activity starts.
Membrane brownfield expansion next to Goa facility under Mann+Hummel technology transfer, expected up by end FY27.
demand_pricing: Q2 order inflow INR 8,130 million, driven by medium-sized opportunities and a Hyundai E&C contract of USD 52.83 million for filtration units in the Middle East at better margins.
Bid pipeline INR 93,700 million, mainly industrial (refining, power, steel), domestic and international.
Specialty Chemicals growth in Q2 (~17%) was mostly volume-led per management; prices have not risen as much as hoped.
Logistics congestion and unpredictable shipping lines to Europe and Africa remain a headwind for chemical exports.
Treatment Solutions Q2 revenue hit by GCC dispatch deferrals due to Middle East crisis and reversal of some revenue to match costs under accounting standards.
Jal Jeevan Mission is less than 10% of Treatment Solutions book; UP Jal Jeevan order INR 2,630 million; government-agency receivables about 10% of total, with dispatches calibrated to fund flows.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Specialty Chemicals margin decline is raw materials vs Roha ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Roha facility impact was about 7% at segment level, West Asia input cost increases not passed on about 7-8%, and the balance from lower exchange gains versus last year; about 18% attributed to these factors.

qa_highlights.question: Are legacy Treatment Solutions losses over, and what margin to expect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost overrun on legacy contracts is fully recorded in Q2, the project is over 90% complete, and it expects no further material adverse impact; margins to return to higher single digits in the balance of the year.

qa_highlights.question: How much Hyundai order revenue lands in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify contract-specific revenue but said a portion is expected in FY27; a clearer year-end outlook to come after next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Roha backward integration and break-even timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said backward integration commissioning is in final phase and should finish within FY27; Roha utilisation is around 25% in its first year, with West Asia input costs and pricing pressure slowing volume ramp.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other current liabilities and operating cash flow weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Unearned revenue rose by about INR 250 crore in the quarter and customer advances rose about INR 50 crore, to just under INR 300 crore in total at September.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory carried at higher input costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inventory is kept low and is largely at the cost of Q2 imports, so H2 flow-through is limited to current costs.

risks_watch: Further legacy contract cost overruns or slippage beyond FY27 despite management's assurance that the bottom has been reached.
Middle East / West Asia crisis affecting input costs, GCC dispatches and shipping to Europe and Africa.
Roha plant ramp-up: pricing acceptance internationally, utilisation and completion of backward integration.
Treatment Solutions H2 revenue concentration: heavy invoicing expected in Q3 and Q4 and dependence on Jal Jeevan fund flows in UP.
Operating cash flow weakness driven by rising unearned revenue and customer advances; watch working capital.
Consumer Products break-even by year-end, which was marginally behind plan in H1.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the legacy-project provisioning being complete and on H2 recovery, but cautious and non-specific on Hyundai order revenue, Roha ramp-up, chemical pricing and consumer break-even timing, with repeated references to geopolitical uncertainty.
key_quotes: we have reached the bottom of the barrel as far as that is concerned.
we have considered that entire impact of the overrun in this quarter's financial numbers.
We should be able to get back to our average margin on the treatment solutions.

adds.what: Roha resin plant backward-integration (commissioning expected by year end)
Membrane brownfield expansion next to Goa facility (Mann+Hummel tech), volumes from FY28

growth.why: Management guides Treatment Solutions FY revenue near FY26 levels with H2 margins back to higher single digits and Engineering revenue back to about INR 1,750 crore, backed by an order book of about INR 29,690 million and Roha backward-integration commissioning by year end; Q2 revenue fell about 8% YoY and EBITDA swung to a loss, so the outlook is only partially evidenced.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides Treatment Solutions margins back to higher single digits in the balance of FY27 after Q2 EBITDA loss of INR 848 mn on INR 6,747 mn revenue, with legacy overrun fully provided; Specialty Chemicals margins under pressure from West Asia input costs and Roha facility costs (about 18% of decline).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Roha backward-integration plant (CWIP about INR 240 crore, commissioning expected by year end) and Goa membrane brownfield (up by end FY27, volumes from FY28) are under construction; Roha resin utilisation only about 25% so the new capacity is not yet a utilisation constraint.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order inflow INR 8,130 mn in Q2 and order book about INR 29,690 mn (30 Sep 2026); Treatment Solutions FY revenue guided near FY26 levels with heavy Q3-Q4 invoicing, though Q2 revenue fell to INR 1,498 mn from INR 2,958 mn and Specialty Chemicals growth was volume-led (~17%).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is low (Roha about 25% in first year) and no new major plant is discussed; the call only references existing projects (Roha, Goa, Ankleshwar modular expansion), so a fresh capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on Hyundai order revenue timing, Roha ramp, chemical pricing (prices 'not risen as much as hoped') and Consumer break-even, and H1 EBITDA was a loss of INR 530 mn, so upgrades look unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Risks include further legacy cost overruns beyond FY27 (legacy contract spilling into FY28), Middle East disruption to GCC dispatches and shipping, Consumer break-even marginally behind plan, and Treatment Solutions H2 revenue dependent on heavy Q3-Q4 invoicing and Jal Jeevan fund flows.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Membrane plant with Mann+Hummel tech tie-up in Goa expected up by end FY27 with volumes from FY28; Hyundai E&C USD 52.83 mn Middle East filtration contract adds product scope but no launch timing was given.

rows.label: Treatment Solutions legacy-project closure and H2 recovery
rows.why: Cost overrun fully provided in Q2 and project over 90% complete, with management guiding H2 margins to higher single digits; however Treatment Solutions Q2 revenue fell to INR 1,498 mn from INR 2,958 mn and EBIT loss was INR 1,215 mn.

rows.label: Operating cash flow and unearned revenue build
rows.why: Unearned revenue rose about INR 250 crore in Q2 and customer advances about INR 50 crore to just under INR 300 crore, which weighed on operating cash flow and may unwind as Treatment Solutions invoicing lands in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: Hyundai E&C Middle East filtration contract
rows.why: USD 52.83 mn contract booked at better margins in Q2; management said a portion lands in FY27 but declined to quantify, with clarity after next quarter.

tone.note: Management was confident that legacy-project provisioning is complete and that H2 Treatment Solutions margins recover, but cautious and non-specific on Hyundai revenue timing, Roha ramp-up, chemical pricing and Consumer break-even, citing Middle East uncertainty; analysts pushed on the margin declin
